title: Do bully sticks go bad? Shelf life and storage | Nibbables
meta: Bully stick shelf life, storage and when to take one away, quoted from 18 brand product pages plus Redbarn, Natural Farm and FDA guidance.
h1: How long do bully sticks last? Shelf life, storage and the last piece, quoted
intro: People ask three different things about how long a bully stick lasts: how long an unopened bag keeps, how to store one your dog has started, and when to take the last piece away. Most brand product pages don't answer the first two, and the brands that do don't always agree. Below, each of the 18 bully stick product pages in our directory is quoted side by side, followed by what guides from Redbarn and three other bully stick sellers, and the FDA, say. Nibbables hasn't tested storage methods or timed any chews; follow the date and instructions on your bag, and ask your vet if you're unsure.

faq.a: Yes, according to the brands that address it. Natural Farm's guide says “Unopened bully sticks last 2-3 years when stored in a cool, dry place below 80°F.” and lists signs to throw one out, including “Mold. White, green, or black fuzzy spots anywhere on the surface.” and “If a stick develops a sour or ammonia-like smell after chewing, it's gone bad. Discard it.” Natural Farm also says: “Always check the best-by date on the bag.”

faq.q: How long can you keep a bully stick?
faq.a: Only 4 of the 18 bully stick product pages in our directory state a shelf life: Pawstruck and Redbarn each say “Shelf Life: 36 months”, Bully Bunches says “Shelf life of 1-2 years.”, and Jack&Pup says only “Properly stored chews will maintain their quality and freshness for months.” The other 14 pages don't say. Two seller guides give ranges for unopened sticks: Natural Farm says 2-3 years, and Bully Sticks Direct says “~18–24 months typical; up to 2–3 years under ideal conditions.” The date printed on your bag is the brand's own answer for that batch.

faq.q: Should you refrigerate a bully stick after your dog chews it?
faq.a: Brands disagree. Redbarn's guide says to “let the bully stick air dry”, then “store the bully stick in a cool, dry place where your pet can’t reach, like a high cabinet or pantry shelf”, and adds: “We do not recommend refrigeration as the moisture could potentially attract bacteria.” Natural Farm says the opposite for a chewed stick: “Once your dog starts chewing one, seal it in an airtight bag, refrigerate, and use within a week.” Bully Sticks Direct says: “Dry and refrigerate chewed sticks, and discard after a couple of days.” Natural Farm and Bully Sticks Direct both sell bully sticks. Follow the brand you bought, and ask your vet if unsure.

faq.q: How long should a bully stick last a dog?
faq.a: None of the 18 product pages we list says how many minutes or days one stick should last. Brutus & Barnaby, a bully stick seller, writes: “Most dogs should chew a bully stick for about 10 to 30 minutes at a time, depending on their size, chewing style, experience level, and stomach sensitivity” and “If your dog is new to bully sticks, start with a short session: 10 to 15 minutes”. Nibbables hasn't timed any chews.

faq.q: When to take a bully stick away?
faq.a: Redbarn's guide says: “Take the bully stick away and discard it once it can be swallowed whole (about 2.5 - 3 inches in most cases).” Brutus & Barnaby says: “When the stick gets small enough to swallow, it is time to take it away”. On the product pages, 11 of 18 say something about the last or broken pieces (see the table): for example Jack&Pup says “Remove the chew if it becomes small enough to swallow or breaks into pieces.” and Raw Paws Pet Food says “If this chew splinters, develops sharp edges or breaks into pieces throw it away immediately.”

sections.h: Bully stick holders for the last piece
sections.p: Redbarn's guide mentions holders: “Some pet owners also use bully stick holders to ensure that their dogs are not able to consume the last portion of a bully stick.” Bow Wow Labs sells one and describes it on its bully stick page (quoted in the table). Nibbables hasn't tested any holder.

sections.h: What the FDA says about storing dry pet food and treats
sections.p: The FDA's pet food handling tips aren't specific to bully sticks, but they cover dry pet food: “Store dry pet food in a cool and dry place. The temperature should be less than 80 F.” and “Store dry pet food in its original bag and keep the top of the bag tightly folded down.” The FDA also says to “wash your hands for at least 20 seconds with soap and hot water” before and after handling pet food and treats.
